root_idea.summary: The supplied evidence supports negation as the central orientation: ليس denies a predicate or asserted state.
root_idea.development: The form is a defective Form I verb whose ordinary predicate-negation may, by context, refer beyond the present and may also acquire generalized force in constructions meaning that there is no such circumstance.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The supplied QAC group represents the Quranic Form I verb ليس and is displayed under its normalized Classical Arabic citation form.

senses.definition: To be not; to negate a predicate or asserted state.
senses.usage_conditions: A defective negative verb, ordinarily used for particular predicate-negation, especially concerning the present state. It governs a nominative subject and an accusative predicate; context can extend the negation to another time, and the verb may also negate a following verbal assertion.

senses.definition: To negate generally or universally: there is no such thing, circumstance, or liability.
senses.usage_conditions: Used in a generalizing negative construction, equivalent in force to لا التبرئة. This includes constructions such as ليس عليكم جناح, in which no blame or liability is asserted.

other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in place of إِلَّا. In this construction, the understood subject is nominative and the predicate is accusative; it may also be followed by a pronoun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A connective negative particle, equivalent to لا in a coordinated or contrastive statement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction may contain a suppressed predicate, so that ليس links a preceding expression with a negated identification or contrast.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Its lexical branches are covered by ordinary and generalized Quranic negation and by the two Classical particle uses.
Pointer-only cross-reference with no independent lexical statement.

cautions: Classical grammatical analysis records disagreement over whether ليس is a defective verb or a particle; QAC identifies the supplied Quranic occurrences as Verb · Form I.
